expected_results: A broker-neutral MANUAL_STAFF withdrawal (no account, no originating event) renders its broker name from exactly ONE owner-matching APPLIED StaffWithdrawalCorrelation decision's broker_profile, while remaining REQUESTED/pending with amount/currency/reference unknown and account UNRESOLVED (no false completion, no fabricated field).

Deterministic precedence preserved: (1) resolved account broker, (2) originating event broker, (3) APPLIED staff-correlation decision broker, (4) blank. Account- (TradersWay) and event- (Pepperstone) resolution are byte-for-byte unchanged and both out-rank the staff-correlation path.

Fail-closed: a non-APPLIED decision, a decision for another withdrawal, a cross-owner decision, conflicting APPLIED brokers, or absent provenance all yield a blank label — never a guess, never cross-tenant leakage.
No N+1: the staff-correlation broker map is ONE bounded, owner-scoped query; the total query count is constant in the number of rows.
Migration-free and read-only: no model/schema change, makemigrations --check clean, the resolver creates/alters/deletes nothing, and public broker statistics / publication state are untouched.
No PII: only the broker PROFILE NAME is read — never a candidate hash, sender address, account number, reason text, raw email body or any other evidence.
actual_results: metrics._staff_correlation_broker_map(owner): one owner-scoped values_list query over StaffWithdrawalCorrelation(status=APPLIED, owner=owner, resulting_withdrawal not null) -> {withdrawal_id: broker_profile.name}; conflicting APPLIED brokers for the same withdrawal drop the entry (fail closed); empty when owner is None.

metrics._row_broker(w, staff_broker=None): precedence account -> event -> staff_broker.get(w.id) -> ''. Default None preserves legacy callers byte-for-byte. withdrawal_history and withdrawal_speed each compute the map ONCE and pass it to every _row_broker call (history selector + rows; speed completed-series + in-progress).
